Because SELinux policy grants binder access to this HAL to a wide client attribute, any uid-0 process in any of those domains (including dumpstate, which is reachable from an unprivileged app via Vulnerability 1) obtains arbitrary command execution. The spawned shell lands in u:r:vendor_qti_init_shell:s0 SELinux context via a policy type_transition, a domain holding all Linux capabilities. This issue affects OxygenOS: from 16.1.0 before 16.1.10.500, from 16.0.0 before 16.0.5.1200, and from 15.0.0 before 15.0.0.2000.

t: DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ) path-migration can lead to use-after-free on multi-threaded deployments.
d: NLnet Labs Unbound, 1.22.0 up to and including version 1.26.1, contains a DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ) lifetime bug reachable by a remote DoQ client under multi-threaded operation. A client-triggered QUIC path migration can enter stream/connection cleanup while a mesh reply still retains a pointer to the DoQ stream. Cleanup frees the DoQ stream and when the pending mesh reply later completes it dereferences a stale pointer leading to a crash.

t: Aggregate DNS name chained pointer decompression work leads to degradation of service.
d: NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.26.1 limits compression-pointer traversal for each individual domain-name operation but has no aggregate inbound decompression-work budget. Many chained compression pointers in a message results in a lot of CPU usage following them. A malicious actor with recursive-query access and control of an ordinarily delegated authority that serves specially crafted replies can exploit the vulnerability and degrade Unbound's general performance.

t: Possible insecure NXDOMAIN for non-existing records under a configured island trust anchor underneath an insecure parent.
d: When NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.26.1 is configured with both a root trust anchor and an additional 'trust-anchor:' for an island-of-security zone whose parent is provably insecure under the root chain, a malicious actor who can deliver one forged NXDOMAIN response for a name inside the island, with the NSEC/SOA RRSIG 'SignerName' set to the insecure parent, tricks Unbound's validator to use the root trust anchor instead, and consecutively the insecure parent, thus causing that record to be treated as insecure and denying existence for records in the trust island.

t: Bypass of a configured island trust anchor underneath an insecure parent from an atacker-controlled NSEC record.
d: When NLnet Labs Unbound 1.0.1 up to and including version 1.26.1 is configured with both a root trust anchor and an additional 'trust-anchor:' for an island-of-security zone whose parent is provably insecure under the root chain, a malicious actor with a forged NSEC reply with the SOA bit cleared can trick Unbound to treat the configured trust island as insecure. This happens because the DNSSEC validator in Unbound accepts and caches the NSEC insecure response bypassing the RRSIG validation that the validator was supposed to do. The acceptance of the NSEC record at the trust anchor apex was allowed due to and old fix for type DS and NSEC queries from clients when trust anchor for that name existed.

t: Possible cache poisoning vulnerability via a cache side-channel exposed by 'unwanted-reply-threshold'
d: In NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.26.1, an observable cache-level side-channel can be exposed with 'unwanted-reply-threshold > 0' configurations (not a default configuration). If a response-like UDP datagram reaches the upstream source port currently used by a recursive query, but its TXID does not match any pending query, Unbound counts the packet as an unwanted reply. When the accumulated count reaches the configured threshold, Unbound clears the worker's RRset cache and message cache. This cache clear action does not destroy the current upstream UDP pending query. Therefore, an external observer can distinguish whether a candidate port matches the current upstream source port by checking whether an existing cached item has been cleared. This is a cache side-channel vulnerability that can be used to probe the upstream source port. Although the attack is not feasible on default configurations and the suggested value (10 million) makes it an ureliable attack on a public resolver, in scenarios where the attacker can keep a concurrent query window alive, the attacker can first filter the source port and then perform birthday-style guessing against the TXID, making cache poisoning a feasible attack path.

t: OnePlus OxygenOS improper neutralization of special elements vulnerability
d: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection') and Missing Authorization vulnerability in OnePlus OxygenOS on Android. Any locally installed Android application, with no permissions declared and no user interaction beyond launching it, can execute arbitrary shell commands as uid 0 in the u:r:dumpstate:s0 SELinux domain. Two defects combine: (a) OnePlus's atlasservice binder interface accepts setEvent(String8 name, String8 value) from any caller without authorization, and (b) one event handler (OplusAtlasLogWriter::handleEvent, matching event name atlas_event_multimedia_audio_dumpsys) copies the caller-supplied value into the system property oplus.audio.dumpinfo.type and starts the root init service audiodumpinfo, which passes that property value unsanitized to system(). This issue affects OxygenOS: from 16.1.0 before 16.1.10.500, from 16.0.0 before 16.0.5.1200, and from 15.0.0 before 15.0.0.2000.

t: Jane Menu < 1.5.1 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Store Config Proxy URL
d: The Jane Menu WordPress plugin before 1.5.1 does not have any capability or nonce checks on one of its form handlers, which is reachable by unauthenticated users, allowing them to bind any published page to a remote document of their choosing. The plugin then fetches that document and outputs its head and body into the page without escaping, so an unauthenticated attacker can run arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any visitor to that page, including an administrator.

t: HappyForms < 1.26.15 - Unauthenticated HTML Injection in Admin Notification Email via client_referer
d: The HappyForms WordPress plugin before 1.26.15 does not sanitise or escape a user-controlled referral value before embedding it in the form notification email, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary HTML into the emails site administrators receive.

t: Contest Gallery < 34.0.1 - Unauthenticated Vote Restriction Bypass via Spoofable Client-IP and Forgeable Voter Identity
d: The Contest Gallery WordPress plugin before 34.0.1 does not reliably validate the visitor identity used to enforce its one-vote-per-entry restriction, trusting a client-supplied request header and an unbound client-generated token, which allows unauthenticated users to bypass the restriction and cast multiple votes for the same contest entry, inflating its vote total.

t: LatePoint < 5.7.5 - Unauthenticated Payment Bypass via 'payment_portion' Parameter
d: The LatePoint WordPress plugin before 5.7.5 does not validate the client-supplied value that determines how much is charged for a booking against the amounts the service and site actually allow, allowing an unauthenticated visitor to make the amount due resolve to zero and obtain a confirmed appointment and a recorded order without completing any payment.

t: Simple Shopping Cart 5.1.3 - 5.3.2 - Contributor+ Price Manipulation via Price Verification Bypass
d: The Simple Shopping Cart WordPress plugin before 5.3.3 does not verify submitted product prices against a value only the site owner can set, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to register attacker-chosen prices for existing products, which any visitor can then use to add those products to the cart at that price.

t: Simple Shopping Cart < 5.3.3 - Unauthenticated Payment Bypass via Unverified PayPal IPN Recipient
d: The Simple Shopping Cart WordPress plugin before 5.3.3 does not verify that a PayPal payment notification is for a payment received by the site owner's PayPal account in its default configuration, allowing unauthenticated attackers to have their orders marked as paid using a payment made to an account they control.

t: Payment Gateway for Telcell < 2.0.5 - Unauthenticated Payment Confirmation Forgery via Empty-Default Merchant Secret
d: The Payment Gateway for Telcell WordPress plugin before 2.0.5 does not verify the authenticity of incoming payment notifications, because the secret used to sign them is empty by default, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a valid notification and mark arbitrary WooCommerce orders as paid. The same handler also marks an attacker-chosen order as failed when given an invalid signature.

t: CMP - Coming Soon & Maintenance 4.1.19 - 4.1.20 - Unauthenticated Maintenance Mode Bypass via Custom URL Whitelist
d: The CMP – Coming Soon & Maintenance WordPress plugin before 4.1.21 does not correctly apply maintenance mode to pages added to its page whitelist by manually entered URL pattern, allowing unauthenticated visitors to view the content of those pages while maintenance mode is active.

t: Podman: goroutine/file-descriptor leak in storage/pkg/archive.applylayer and applyuncompressedlayer on malformed layers
d: storage/pkg/archive.ApplyLayer and ApplyUncompressedLayer may, when processing corrupt or malicious inputs, leak a file descriptor; unbounded repeated calls can exhaust the process’ file descriptor limit

t: JITServer: Multiple Denial of Service vulnerabilities via out-of-bounds heap reads during message and reply parsing
d: In Eclipse OpenJ9 versions up to 0.63.0, the JITServer component is vulnerable to denial of service due to improper boundary checks during protocol message and reply handling. An unauthenticated remote attacker or malicious JITServer can transmit malformed network payloads that cause out-of-bounds heap reads, immediately crashing the JITServer daemon or client JVM process via a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV).

t: JITServer: Pre-authentication remote crash via integer underflow and out-of-bounds heap read in DataDescriptor deserialization
d: In Eclipse OpenJ9 versions prior to 0.63.0, the JITServer component fails to perform cross-field validation on attacker-controlled `_size`, `_paddingSize`, and `_dataOffset` fields during `DataDescriptor` message deserialization. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a crafted network payload that triggers an unsigned integer underflow in `DataDescriptor::getPayloadSize()` and `DataDescriptor::getNextDescriptor()`. This results in an out-of-bounds heap read and an immediate process crash (SIGSEGV), causing a denial of service.

t: WordPress Ninja Forms plugin <= 3.15.5 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Kevin Stover Ninja Forms ninja-forms allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Ninja Forms: from n/a through 3.15.5.

t: WordPress Strong Testimonials plugin <= 3.3.12 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WP Chill Strong Testimonials strong-testimonials allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Strong Testimonials: from n/a through 3.3.12.

t: Lm-evaluation-harness: lm-evaluation-harness: ssrf via job-spec model.url with bearer credential forwarding
d: A flaw was found in the `lm-evaluation-harness` component of Red Hat OpenShift AI. An authenticated user, able to submit an evaluation job, could exploit this by providing a malicious model URL in the `JobSpec`. This vulnerability allows for the disclosure of the tenant's model authentication secret to an attacker-controlled external listener. Additionally, it enables Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks against internal network endpoints reachable from the evaluation job pod.

t: JITServer: Pre-authentication remote Denial of Service via integer overflow infinite loop in MessageBuffer::computeRequiredCapacity()
d: In Eclipse OpenJ9 versions prior to 0.63.0, the JITServer component is vulnerable to a pre-authentication remote denial of service. When processing the initial 4-byte length field of an incoming TCP connection, an integer overflow in `MessageBuffer::computeRequiredCapacity()` causes the receiving compilation worker thread to enter an infinite loop consuming ~100% CPU. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by opening a small number of crafted TCP connections to exhaust the entire worker thread pool, silently halting compilation services for all connected client JVMs.

t: Cart Abandonment Recovery for WooCommerce < 2.2.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Unsigned Recovery Token
d: The Cart Abandonment Recovery for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 2.2.0 does not verify the integrity of its cart-recovery token before acting on it and still accepts an unsigned legacy token format, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a victim's cart session identifier to modify that victim's abandoned-cart record, for example unsubscribing them from recovery emails or applying an arbitrary coupon to their restored cart.

t: Click n Chat 1.0.4 - 1.1.2 - Unauthenticated Lead Data Disclosure via click_n_chat_update_lead_list_export_action
d: The Click n Chat (Chat Widget Integration) WordPress plugin before 1.1.3 does not perform any authorization check on a lead-export handler, allowing unauthenticated users to download every captured contact record (names, email addresses and phone numbers).

t: Click n Chat 1.0.4 - 1.1.2 - Unauthenticated SQLi via 'sort_by'/'sort_order' Parameters
d: The Click n Chat (Chat Widget Integration) WordPress plugin before 1.1.3 does not sanitise sort parameters before using them in a SQL ORDER BY clause, allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform SQL injection attacks.

t: Click n Chat < 1.1.3 - Unauthenticated SQLi via 'datacolumn' Parameter
d: The Click n Chat (Chat Widget Integration) WordPress plugin before 1.1.3 does not properly validate a parameter before using it as a column identifier in a SQL query, allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform SQL injection attacks.

t: Weglot < 6.4.3 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Translated Page Link Rewriting
d: The Translate WordPress with Weglot 2.0 WordPress plugin before 6.4.3 does not escape the URLs it re-inserts into a page when rewriting links for a translated language, and reverses the encoding that was applied to them beforehand, allowing unauthenticated users to store a payload which executes in the browser of anyone viewing the page in a translated language.

t: Wava Payment 0.3.1 - 0.3.9 - Unauthenticated Merchant Credential Overwrite via Install Webhook
d: The Wava Payment Plugin WordPress plugin before 0.3.10 does not perform any authorisation, nonce or origin verification on one of its public REST endpoints, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the stored credential that identifies the merchant account the store's payments are created against, to force the integration into a verified state the site owner never completed, and to remove the payment method from the store's checkout.

t: Wava Payment 0.3.1 - 0.3.9 - Unauthenticated Order Status Change via Payment Webhook
d: The Wava Payment Plugin WordPress plugin before 0.3.10 does not verify the authenticity of incoming payment-provider notifications, nor restrict who may send them, allowing unauthenticated attackers to change the status of any WooCommerce order in the store, including marking an unpaid order as paid and completed, and cancelling other customers' orders. In versions up to 0.3.7 the response additionally returns the affected order's billing details, disclosing customer names, addresses, email addresses and phone numbers to the same unauthenticated caller.

t: Download Manager (Free & Pro) - Privacy Settings Update via CSRF
d: The Download Manager WordPress plugin before 3.3.71, Download Manager WordPress plugin before 7.5.9 does not have CSRF checks in some places, allowing attackers to make a logged in admin update its privacy and storage settings via a crafted link, including the credential that gates its unauthenticated maintenance endpoint.

t: Formidable Forms 6.5 - 6.35 - Unauthenticated Payment Gateway Connect Verification DoS
d: The Formidable Forms WordPress plugin before 7.0 does not verify the identity of the caller before recording the timestamp it uses to rate limit payment gateway verification requests, allowing unauthenticated attackers to consume the daily allowance and cause legitimate verification attempts to be refused for the next 24 hours.

t: Elementor < 4.3.5 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via SVG CDATA Sanitizer Bypass
d: The Elementor Website Builder WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not sanitize the text content of SVG files, checking only their elements and attributes, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to store a payload which breaks out when the SVG is rendered inline in a page and executes in the browser of any user viewing it. Execution is specific to Chromium-based browsers; Firefox is not affected.

t: Elementor < 4.3.5 - Author+ Stored XSS via SVG Upload
d: The Elementor Website Builder WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not sanitize uploaded SVG files on every upload route, allowing users with the Author role and above to upload a file containing JavaScript, which will run in the browser of any user who opens it. Exploitation requires unfiltered file uploads to be enabled in the Elementor Website Builder WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 settings, which is not the default.

t: Advanced File Manager 5.4.13 - 5.4.14 - Authenticated Stored XSS via SVG Sanitiser Content-Sniff Bypass
d: The Advanced File Manager WordPress plugin before 6.0.0 does not correctly determine whether a stored file is an SVG before sanitising it, allowing users granted file-manager access by an administrator to store a file containing script that is not stripped and that runs in the browser of anyone who opens it, including an administrator.

t: TI WooCommerce Wishlist < 2.13.0 - Unauthenticated Private Wishlist Disclosure via share_key
d: The TI WooCommerce Wishlist WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not enforce the same owner-only access control on its REST API that it applies on the front-end, allowing unauthenticated users to read the metadata and item contents of private wishlists.

t: SUMIT Payment Gateway for WooCommerce < 4.0.0 - Unauthenticated Payment Confirmation Forgery via Redirect Callback
d: The SUMIT Payment Gateway for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 4.0.0 does not bind the payment it confirms with the provider to the order being completed, nor check the payment amount against the order total, allowing unauthenticated users to mark a pending order as paid by replaying a payment identifier obtained from any single genuine payment.

t: WholesaleX < 3.0.9 - Unauthenticated Imported User CSV Disclosure
d: The WholesaleX WordPress plugin before 3.0.9 does not protect or remove the user-import file it keeps in a publicly accessible location under a predictable name, allowing unauthenticated users to download the most recently imported user data, including any account passwords and customer contact and address details it contains.

t: WholesaleX < 3.0.9 - Unauthenticated Account Activation and Administrator Approval Bypass
d: The WholesaleX WordPress plugin before 3.0.9 does not check that a stored account confirmation code is set before comparing it with the one supplied in a request, allowing unauthenticated users to activate pending accounts and bypass the administrator approval required before login.

t: miniOrange 2FA 6.2.9 - 6.3.0 - 2FA Bypass via Passkey Second-Factor Rebinding
d: The miniOrange 2FA WordPress plugin before 6.3.1 does not prevent a pending passkey login from registering an additional passkey on an account that already has one configured, allowing an attacker who knows a user's password to add their own authenticator and bypass the second factor.

t: Profile Builder < 4.0.1 - Reflected XSS via Unconfirmed Emails Row Actions
d: The User Profile Builder WordPress plugin before 4.0.1 does not escape the current page URL before outputting it in a JavaScript context on one of its admin pages, leading to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting against high-privilege users.

t: Easy Pricing Tables < 4.1.3 - Contributor+ Arbitrary Post Clone and Publish via Legacy Table Duplication
d: The Pricing Table WordPress Plugin WordPress plugin before 4.1.3 does not perform authorisation checks when duplicating a legacy pricing table, allowing users with the contributor role and above to clone and publish any post or page on the site, including private and draft content belonging to other users.

t: Kliken: Ads + Pixel for Meta < 1.2.3 - Unauthenticated Order Data Disclosure via IDOR
d: The Kliken: Ads + Pixel for Meta WordPress plugin before 1.2.3 does not verify that a visitor holds an order's key before outputting that order's details on the order confirmation page, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve the billing location, purchased products and totals of other customers' orders by enumerating order IDs.

t: Redirection for Contact Form 7 2.2.7 - 3.2.11 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Lead Debug Metabox
d: The Redirection for Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 3.2.12 does not sanitise or escape submitted form data stored as lead entries before outputting it in the lead debug metabox, allowing unauthenticated attackers to store a malicious script that executes when a logged-in user views the entry with the Redirection for Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 3.2.12's debug mode enabled.

t: AI Engine < 3.8.6 - Editor+ Arbitrary Post Title and Excerpt Update via update_post_title and update_post_excerpt
d: The AI Engine WordPress plugin before 3.8.6 does not check that the caller is allowed to edit the targeted object before updating its title and excerpt, allowing users with the Editor role and above to modify arbitrary posts of any type, including content they cannot otherwise edit such as navigation menus, block templates, global styles and WooCommerce coupons.

t: Swift Performance Lite < 2.3.7.4 - Author+ SQLi via Image Optimizer
d: The Swift Performance Lite WordPress plugin before 2.3.7.4 does not properly sanitize and escape a value before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow users with the author role and above to perform SQL injection attacks.

t: WP User Manager 2.9.21 - 2.9.25 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Paid Registration Role After Stripe Disconnect
d: The WP User Manager WordPress plugin before 2.9.26 does not keep its paid-registration capability restrictions in force once the payment gateway is disconnected, while a published paid registration form continues to assign its configured role, allowing unauthenticated users to register and immediately obtain a privileged administrator-equivalent role without completing the payment meant to gate it.

t: WPZOOM Portfolio < 1.4.34 - Contributor+ Arbitrary Post/Page Type Overwrite via IDOR
d: The WPZOOM Portfolio Lite WordPress plugin before 1.4.34 does not check that a user is allowed to edit a post before changing its type and order, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to convert any other user's posts and pages into portfolio items, removing them from their original listings and URLs.

t: Productive Commerce < 1.1.49 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary Plugin Activation
d: The Productive Commerce WordPress plugin before 1.1.49 does not perform a capability check in one of its AJAX actions and exposes the nonce that guards it on every admin-area page, allowing any authenticated user such as a subscriber to activate arbitrary Productive Commerce WordPress plugin before 1.1.49 already installed on the site.

t: WP Booking System < 2.1.0.3 - Reflected XSS via 'booking_id' Parameter
d: The WP Booking System WordPress plugin before 2.1.0.3 does not validate and escape one of its parameters before reflecting it back in an admin page, leading to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high privilege users such as administrators.

t: SureCart < 4.9.5 - Unauthenticated Private Catalog Data Disclosure via 'expand' Parameter
d: The SureCart WordPress plugin before 4.9.5 does not restrict which related objects an anonymous visitor may include when reading a single upsell funnel through its REST API, nor strip private fields from those objects, allowing unauthenticated users to read merchant-private catalog data such as pricing, commission, stock, SKU and tax internals, including unpublished products.

t: WP Job Openings < 4.1.1 - Author+ Stored XSS via Job Title
d: The HireZoot WordPress plugin before 4.1.1 does not sanitise and escape some of its stored data before outputting it in the admin dashboard, and additionally reverses the HTML-entity encoding that would otherwise neutralise it, allowing users with the Author role to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks that execute in the context of a logged-in administrator.

t: SmartyParcel < 1.23.4 - Unauthenticated Shipping Label Disclosure via IDOR
d: The SmartyParcel WordPress plugin before 1.23.4 does not perform authorisation checks when serving shipping label downloads, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the shipping labels of arbitrary orders, which contain customer names, addresses and phone numbers.

t: SmartyParcel (WC Ukr Shipping) < 1.23.4 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary Shipping Label Deletion
d: The SmartyParcel WordPress plugin before 1.23.4 does not perform authorisation checks when deleting shipping label records, allowing any authenticated user such as a subscriber to delete the shipping label and tracking records of arbitrary orders store-wide.

t: Simple Banner < 3.3.3 - Authenticated Privilege Escalation via User Permissions Setting
d: The Simple Banner WordPress plugin before 3.3.3 does not correctly limit the capabilities it grants to the user roles an administrator allows to manage its banners, granting such roles the full administrator capability, which allows users in a low-privileged role to escalate their privileges and fully compromise the site.

t: Backup and Staging by WP Time Capsule < 1.22.28 - Subscriber+ Staging-to-Live Deployment via wptc_copy_stage_to_live
d: The Backup and Staging by WP Time Capsule WordPress plugin before 1.22.28 does not perform capability or nonce checks on the handler that deploys a staging site to the live site, allowing any authenticated user with a Subscriber account on a WP Time Capsule staging site to overwrite the separate live site's database and configuration and take it offline.
r: Backup and Staging by WP Time Capsule

t: Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash < 3.8.2 - Admin+ Cross-Site Account Lockout via Missing Authorization
d: The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash WordPress plugin before 3.8.2 does not verify that the acting user is permitted to manage the targeted accounts before changing their verification state, allowing a subsite administrator on a multisite network to mark arbitrary network users outside their own site as unverified and prevent those users from logging in.

t: Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash < 3.8.2 - Account Takeover via Password Reset CSRF
d: The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash WordPress plugin before 3.8.2 does not validate the origin of a password-reset request, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to set the password of a user who is partway through a password reset to an attacker-chosen value through a forged request, resulting in full account takeover.

t: Moloni < 5.0.14 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary Order Invoice Generation via genInvoice
d: The Moloni WordPress plugin before 5.0.14 does not perform capability or nonce checks on several of its authenticated AJAX actions, relying only on whether the site holds a stored connection to its external invoicing provider, allowing any authenticated user such as a Subscriber to generate fiscal invoices for arbitrary orders, discard arbitrary orders, and create or modify products and stock.

t: Booking Package < 1.7.31 - Unauthenticated Calendar Account Information Disclosure
d: The Booking Package WordPress plugin before 1.7.31 does not perform authorization checks before returning calendar-account configuration in a response, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose sensitive settings including the administrator's notification email addresses.

t: Booking Package < 1.7.31 - Unauthenticated Subscription Deactivation via Missing Authorization
d: The Booking Package WordPress plugin before 1.7.31 does not perform any authorization or validity check before resetting its premium subscription state, allowing unauthenticated attackers to disable the Booking Package WordPress plugin before 1.7.31's paid features.

t: Booking Package < 1.7.31 - Unauthenticated Booking PII Disclosure and Cancellation via Predictable Token
d: The Booking Package WordPress plugin before 1.7.31 does not generate booking cancellation tokens using a secure source of randomness, deriving them instead from values it exposes publicly, so an unauthenticated attacker can reconstruct an arbitrary booking's token, disclose that booking's personal data and, where visitor cancellation is enabled, cancel the booking.

t: Ettrick Escape Room Booking < 1.3.1 - Unauthenticated Payment Confirmation Bypass
d: The Ettrick Escape Room Booking WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not verify a booking's payment status against the payment provider before marking it paid and confirmed, allowing unauthenticated attackers to mark bookings as paid without paying.

t: Falang multilanguage for WordPress < 1.4.6 - Subscriber+ Stored XSS via Term Translation
d: The Falang multilanguage for WordPress plugin before 1.4.6 does not perform a capability check when saving term translations, and exposes a valid nonce to any logged-in user through an unprotected handler, allowing users with Subscriber-level access and above to store content that is later output without proper escaping, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the context of higher-privileged users such as administrators.

t: LatePoint < 5.7.5 - Agent+ Customer PII Disclosure via IDOR
d: The Appointment Booking Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.7.5 does not verify that an authenticated agent-level user is assigned to a customer before returning or searching that customer's record, allowing any agent to read and enumerate the personal information of every customer on the site, including those managed by other agents.

t: Payment Gateway for Idram < 2.1.6 - Unauthenticated Payment Confirmation Forgery via Empty-Default Merchant Secret
d: The Payment Gateway for Idram WordPress plugin before 2.1.6 does not verify the authenticity of incoming payment notifications, because the merchant credentials used to compute their checksum are empty by default, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a valid payment confirmation and mark arbitrary orders as paid, and to force arbitrary orders into a failed state regardless of the gateway's configuration.

t: Modern Events Calendar (Lite & Pro) < 7.37.0 - Subscriber+ SQLi via mec_attendees AJAX Action
d: The Modern Events Calendar Lite WordPress plugin before 7.37.0, Modern Event Calendar Pro WordPress plugin before 7.37.0 do not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which allows authenticated users with Subscriber-level access and above to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries and extract sensitive data from the database.

t: Synchrony Financing 1.0.5 - 1.1.1 - Unauthenticated Order Takeover via admin_order_callback REST Route
d: The Synchrony Financing WordPress plugin before 1.1.2 does not properly authorise requests to one of its REST routes that modifies WooCommerce orders, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reassign any order to an account they control, tamper with its details, and read the associated customer's personal data.

In OpenStack Cinder through 29.0.0, cross-project information disclosure can occur in the Messages API. A non-admin user with the project-scoped 'member' or 'reader' role making the Block Storage API v3.3 "List messages" call finds the non-expired user messages for other projects included in the response, resulting in the leakage of UUIDs of resources owned by other projects, in addition to the user message about the other projects' resources (which, by design, are sanitized generic messages). All Cinder deployments are affected.

In OpenStack Manila before 23.0.1, multiple Manila API operations on public shares do not verify that the caller owns the share. The API controllers authorize operations against the caller's own project context, then load a foreign public share without re-authorizing against the share's actual owner. This affects the following operations: allow_access: grant data-plane read/write access to another tenant's share; deny_access: revoke the owner's existing access rules; update_access: escalate access level (e.g., ro to rw); create_share_backup: exfiltrate share data via a backup created under the attacker's project; soft_delete: move a foreign share to the recycle bin; restore: interfere with the owner's deletion workflow; export location metadata: create, update, and delete metadata on foreign export locations; access rule listing: disclose IPs, usernames, and CephFS keys. Any authenticated project member can exploit these operations on any public share. The share UUID is visible since the share is public.

t: Universal Naming Convention (UNC) Path Injection in Cerberus FTP Server
d: A vulnerability in Cerberus FTP Server allows an authenticated remote attacker to perform UNC path injection via a manipulated parameter. By supplying a malicious SMB share path, an attacker can execute authentication coercion against the underlying server, resulting in the leakage of the Cerberus service account's Net-NTLMv2 hash. This issue has been resolved in Cerberus FTP Server: 2026.3.0.

t: DT42 BerryNet Model Package Metadata dlmodelmgr.py DLModelManager.get_model_meta path traversal
d: A security vulnerability has been detected in DT42 BerryNet up to 3.10.2. The affected element is the function DLModelManager.get_model_meta of the file berrynet/dlmodelmgr.py of the component Model Package Metadata Handler. The manipulation of the argument label leads to path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

t: projectworlds Advanced Library Management System report_search.php mysqli_query sql injection
d: A weakness has been identified in projectworlds Advanced Library Management System 1.0. Impacted is the function mysqli_query of the file report_search.php. Executing a manipulation of the argument dateto/datefrom can lead to sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

t: Libmodulemd: libmodulemd: out-of-bounds read when emitting rpm-map artifacts
d: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. In the module stream v2 rpm-map emission path, an inner loop incorrectly uses the count of digest algorithms as its bound instead of the number of checksums in the current digest table. Crafted modulemd v2 metadata with multiple digest types can trigger an out-of-bounds read during YAML serialization, typically causing a crash and resulting in a denial of service.

t: Libmodulemd: libmodulemd: missing decompressed-size limit when parsing compressed yaml
d: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. In builds with rpmio support enabled, compressed modulemd YAML is decompressed through a custom read handler that does not enforce a cumulative decompressed-size limit before parsing. An attacker who can supply a highly compressible compressed YAML file can cause excessive CPU and memory consumption, resulting in a denial of service.

t: Libmodulemd: libmodulemd: unbounded recursion when parsing nested xmd yaml
d: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. When parsing module metadata, the xmd field is converted into nested GVariant values through recursive YAML mapping and sequence helpers without a recursion-depth or node-count limit. An attacker who can supply crafted modulemd YAML with deeply nested xmd content can cause stack exhaustion or excessive resource consumption, resulting in a denial of service.

t: Duplicator <= 1.5.17 and Duplicator Pro <= 4.6.10 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection
d: The Duplicator and Duplicator Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.17 and 4.6.10, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted database content in DUPX_UpdateEngine::unserializeTest() during migration. This allows unauthenticated attackers to store a serialized object in public site content before an administrator builds a package and later performs a migration or import that runs database search-and-replace. Duplicator Free bundles a Requests 1.7 POP chain that permits attacker-selected callbacks, resulting in direct operating-system command execution. Duplicator Pro bundles an IndexList destructor gadget that permits deletion of an attacker-selected existing file when its containing directory is writable by the installer PHP process; deletion of wp-config.php can expose the setup wizard and lead to site takeover and code execution if the attacker reaches it first and supplies a reachable database they control. The package must be created after the carrier is stored, and a later administrator migration action is required.
r: Duplicator – Backups & Migration Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups, & More

t: Tenda AC19 httpd Web Management Service SetFirewallCfg formSetFirewallCfg stack-based overflow
d: A security vulnerability has been detected in Tenda AC19 16.03.10.07. The impacted element is the function formSetFirewallCfg of the file /goform/SetFirewallCfg of the component httpd Web Management Service. Such manipulation of the argument firewallEn leads to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

t: Tenstorrent tt-metal load_checkpoints.py load_hf_state_dict_filtered path traversal
d: A weakness has been identified in Tenstorrent tt-metal up to 0.80.0. The affected element is the function load_hf_state_dict_filtered of the file models/tt_transformers/tt/load_checkpoints.py. This manipulation of the argument weight_map causes path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 0.81.0-dev20261016 is sufficient to fix this issue. Patch name: 4851ccf347f6903c3d819eed60705600386e52c3. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

t: OS Command Injection in Qingteng Host Adaptive Security Platform Security Toolbox
d: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command in Security Toolbox versions before 20260929 in Qingteng Host Adaptive Security Platform (Host Monitoring) V3.0 allows an authenticated console administrator to execute arbitrary commands on attached clients via OS command injection

t: itsourcecode Online Cake Ordering System 404.php cross site scripting
d: A vulnerability has been found in itsourcecode Online Cake Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file /404.php. Such manipulation of the argument useruid leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

t: Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509
d: On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action. To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

t: itsourcecode Online Cake Ordering System deletecustomer.php sql injection
d: A flaw has been found in itsourcecode Online Cake Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file /deletecustomer.php. This manipulation of the argument ID causes sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

t: Deserialization of untrusted data in floss
d: Deserialization of untrusted data in Mandiant FLARE floss releases before 3.2.0 allows arbitrary code execution when a crafted .viv or .exe.viv workspace is passed to the floss utility

t: Deserialization of untrusted data in capa
d: Deserialization of untrusted data in Mandiant FLARE capa releases before 10.0.0 allows arbitrary code execution when a crafted .viv or .exe.viv workspace is passed to the capa utility

t: Best Practice Software Bp Premier before 1.14.1.1128 Hardcoded SQL Server Administrative Credential
d: Best Practice Software Bp Premier before 1.14.1.1128 uses a hardcoded Microsoft SQL Server administrative password that is shared across all installations and cannot be changed without breaking the application. Attackers with network access to the database instance can authenticate as sysadmin, bypass application authentication, and execute operating system commands as SYSTEM.

t: Vyper 0.3.4 through 0.5.0b1 create_from_blueprint Offset Validation Bypass via Unsigned Wraparound
d: Vyper 0.3.4 through 0.5.0b1 computes the remaining blueprint size in create_from_blueprint by uint256 subtraction without first checking that code_offset is below the blueprint's code size, so a huge offset wraps to a small positive value. An attacker controlling code_offset can make a factory deploy contracts with no runtime code, potentially trapping ETH and tokens.

t: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 Optimizer Miscompilation of msg.value | K in Ternary Branches
d: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains an optimizer miscompilation in which (msg.value | K) or (len(msg.data) | K), where K is any nonzero integer literal, is compiled to the constant 1 when used as a ternary expression branch under -O gas (the default) or -O codesize. Affected contracts use the wrong value in storage writes, arithmetic, indexes, return values, or events without warning or revert, which can record deposits incorrectly and lock funds.

t: Vyper through 0.5.0b1 Literal Value Manipulation via Line Separators
d: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b17 and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 builds its source-line table with str.splitlines(), which treats characters like form feed and U+2028 as line breaks the Python parser ignores, so numeric literals are classified and validated from shifted source text. An attacker contributing source code can hide these characters in comments, strings or indentation to silently change address, integer or decimal constants.

t: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 Memory Misread via Ternary Nested Array Selection
d: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains a compiler miscompilation vulnerability in parse_IfExp that reads nested arrays with narrower inner bounds using the wider result type's memory layout. When a ternary selects the narrower array, inner arrays after the first are read at wrong offsets, causing contracts to silently store corrupted values or revert.

t: Vyper through 0.5.0b1 Literal Value Substitution via Multi-byte Characters
d: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b12, 0.1.0b14, and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 mix character-based line offsets with Python's UTF-8 byte col_offset values in vyper/ast/parse.py, so multi-byte characters shift the source slices used to reconstruct later numeric literals. An attacker contributing source with non-ASCII identifiers that NFKC-normalize to ASCII, or an invisible byte-order mark, can silently substitute addresses, integers or other constants in compiled code.

t: Sharp before 0.35.0 Multiple Vulnerabilities via Bundled libvips Image Decoders
d: Sharp before 0.35.0 bundles a version of libvips affected by multiple vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-33327, CVE-2026-33328, CVE-2026-35590, CVE-2026-35591 and CVE-2026-69242) in its GIF, TIFF and VIPS image decoders. Attackers can supply crafted GIF, TIFF or VIPS files to applications using sharp to process untrusted input, triggering these libvips flaws.

t: Sharp before 0.35.4 RCE via bundled libheif AVIF decoding
d: Sharp before 0.35.4 bundles a vulnerable libheif dependency that allows attackers to achieve possible remote code execution on glibc-based Linux by supplying crafted images. Attackers can submit malicious AVIF/HEIF input to applications processing untrusted images with sharp, triggering libheif decoding flaws to execute code.

t: Sharp before 0.35.5 RCE via librsvg Dependency Memory Vulnerability
d: sharp before 0.35.5 bundles a librsvg dependency affected by a memory-related vulnerability (CVE-2026-96889) that, under certain runtime-specific conditions, can lead to code execution on glibc-based Linux. An attacker can supply a crafted SVG image that, when decoded by sharp through librsvg, may result in arbitrary code execution.

t: Astral uv before 0.11.6 Arbitrary File Deletion via Wheel RECORD Entries
d: Astral uv before 0.11.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to delete arbitrary files by supplying wheels with relative traversal paths in RECORD entries. Attackers can craft a malicious wheel whose RECORD references files outside the installation prefix, causing uv to delete those files when the user uninstalls the package.

t: uv before 0.11.15 Arbitrary File Write via Entry Point Names
d: uv before 0.11.15 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious wheels to write files outside the scripts directory via crafted console_scripts or gui_scripts entry point names. Attackers who induce users to install a malicious wheel can place executables in PATH directories, shadowing or overwriting existing binaries for code execution.

t: HKUDS Vibe-Trading before 0.1.7 Missing Authentication in FastAPI Server Enabling RCE
d: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access the FastAPI surface because require_auth() returns early when API_AUTH_KEY is unset. Attackers can post messages to /sessions/{id}/messages to trigger root shell commands via BashTool, upload .py or .sh files via /upload, read session histories, and obtain partial API keys.

t: HKUDS Vibe-Trading 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 Indirect Prompt Injection RCE via BashTool and BackgroundRunTool
d: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains an indirect prompt injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute shell commands as root by planting instructions in documents or web pages the agent processes. BashTool and BackgroundRunTool pass model-emitted commands to subprocess.run with shell=True and no allow-list or approval step, and read_url fetches arbitrary URLs, enabling command execution and server-side request forgery.

t: HKUDS Vibe-Trading 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 Path Traversal via read_document and safe_user_path
d: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to read sensitive server files through LLM agent file-read tools. Attackers can prompt the agent to invoke read_document, which lacks sandbox checks, or safe_user_path-gated tools to leak /etc/shadow, /proc/self/environ API keys, and /root credentials.

t: Adm-zip before 0.6.1 Privilege Escalation via keepOriginalPermission Setuid Bits
d: Adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows attackers to set setuid, setgid, or sticky bits on extracted files when keepOriginalPermission is enabled. Attackers can craft zip external file attributes that pass unmasked into chmod, letting attacker-controlled executables gain elevated privileges when extracted as root and later run.

t: adm-zip before 0.6.1 Duplicate ZIP Entry Name Validation Bypass
d: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an inconsistent entry resolution vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass content validation by supplying ZIP archives with duplicate entry names. Attackers can craft archives where getEntry() returns the last duplicate while extractAllTo() writes the first, causing unvalidated bytes to be written to disk.

t: adm-zip 0.6.0 Decompression Bomb Guard Bypass via getDataAsync()
d: adm-zip 0.6.0 contains a decompression bomb protection bypass that allows attackers to evade the maxOutputLength guard by targeting the asynchronous getDataAsync() path in methods/inflater.js. Attackers can craft ZIP entries with falsified small declared sizes and high-ratio DEFLATE payloads to exhaust memory in applications reading entries asynchronously.

t: adm-zip before 0.6.1 Denial of Service via inflateAsync Unhandled Error Event
d: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the Node.js process via a malformed ZIP file, because inflateAsync in methods/inflater.js lacks a zlib stream error listener. Attackers can supply a ZIP with corrupted DEFLATE data processed by readFileAsync, readAsTextAsync, extractAllToAsync, or getDataAsync, triggering an uncatchable exception that terminates all in-flight requests.

t: Coraza before 3.8.1 Multipart filename* Charset Handling FILES Rule Bypass
d: Coraza before 3.8.1 extracts multipart upload filenames with Go's mime.ParseMediaType, which silently ignores RFC 5987 filename* parameters whose charset is not utf-8 or us-ascii. Unauthenticated attackers can send a decoy filename with filename*=iso-8859-1''shell.php, or filename* alone, so FILES-based rules never see the real name, letting dangerous uploads reach backends that honor filename*.

t: Coraza from 3.0.4 before 3.8.1 Request Body Inspection Bypass via Content-Type
d: Coraza from 3.0.4 before 3.8.1 contains a request body inspection bypass because request-body processor selection compares the entire Content-Type value exactly, so URL-encoded bodies whose Content-Type carries a media-type parameter are never parsed. Unauthenticated attackers can send application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8 to keep ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY empty, evading body rules while the backend still processes the payload.

t: Coraza 3.0.0 before 3.8.1 WAF Bypass via JSON Key Collision
d: Coraza from 3.0.0 before 3.8.1 has a JSON body processor that flattens nested properties into dot-separated ARGS_POST names without escaping literal dots, so distinct properties collide. Unauthenticated attackers can add a later dotted property such as account.role that overwrites a malicious nested value, hiding SQL injection payloads from OWASP CRS rules while backends still receive them.

t: Dulwich 0.22.5 before 1.2.8 Path Traversal via Stash Pop Symlinks
d: Dulwich from 0.22.5 before 1.2.8 contains a path traversal vulnerability in stash.py pop() that allows attackers to write arbitrary files outside the worktree through intermediate directory symlinks. Attackers can craft a malicious repository whose popped stash writes a payload into .git/hooks/post-checkout, achieving code execution on the next checkout.

t: Dulwich 0.23.1 before 1.2.8 Symlink Path Traversal via filter_branch Index Filter
d: Dulwich from 0.23.1 before 1.2.8 contains a path traversal vulnerability in CommitFilter._apply_index_filter() that allows attackers to write files outside the working directory via symlinks persisting between commits. Attackers can craft a repository where an ancestor commit's symlink redirects a descendant commit's file writes during filter_branch, enabling code execution by writing into .git/hooks.

t: Dulwich 0.24.0 before 1.2.8 Symlink Write-Through via porcelain.checkout paths
d: Dulwich from 0.24.0 before 1.2.8 contains a symlink following vulnerability in porcelain.checkout(paths=[...]) that allows attackers to write arbitrary files by abusing raw os.open without O_NOFOLLOW. Attackers can craft a repository where a worktree symlink points to .git/hooks/post-checkout, so restoring the file from a tag writes a malicious hook for code execution.

t: Dulwich before 1.2.9 Infinite Loop DoS via Pack.resolve_object
d: Dulwich before 1.2.9 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Pack.resolve_object that allows attackers to cause infinite recursion via self-referential OFS_DELTA objects. Attackers can supply a malicious packfile with an OFS_DELTA delta_offset of 0 to exhaust CPU during clone, fetch, or cat-file operations.

t: Dulwich before 1.2.9 Arbitrary File Write via DOS drive letter paths
d: Dulwich before 1.2.9 fails to validate DOS drive letter prefixes in Git tree path elements on Windows, allowing arbitrary file write. Attackers can craft a malicious repository with a tree entry named 'C:' that bypasses NTFS validation and writes files outside the worktree to achieve remote code execution.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Cross-Site Request Forgery via /logout Endpoint
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to log out authenticated users by sending a link to the GET-based /logout endpoint. Attackers can lure victims into clicking an obfuscated, URL-encoded link that terminates their session, causing loss of unsaved work.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 Missing Authentication in Dashboard Run Replay Action
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 performs no authentication or organization check in the action handler of the dashboard run replay route (resources.taskruns.$runParam.replay) and looks up the run by friendlyId alone. A remote attacker who knows a victim's run friendlyId can replay it into an environment of their choosing, exposing the victim's task payload or running the task again with the victim's secrets.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 Cross-Tenant Run Payload Disclosure via API Replay Route
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 looks up runs by friendlyId alone in the api.v1.runs.$runParam.replay route without scoping the lookup to the caller's runtime environment. An attacker holding any tenant's API key who knows a victim's run friendlyId can replay that run into their own environment and read the victim's task payload.

t: Trigger.dev CLI 3.0.0 before 4.5.4 Missing Authentication in MCP Server
d: Trigger.dev cli-v3 from 3.0.0 before 4.5.4 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the trigger dev --mcp server, which binds all network interfaces and exposes the /sse and /messages endpoints. LAN attackers or malicious web pages can send MCP tools/call requests to invoke trigger-task, cancel-run, list-runs, and get-run-logs using the developer's stored access token.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 CLI Auth-Code Phishing Leading to PAT Takeover
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the CLI authorization-code flow because loading /account/authorization-code/<code> mints a Personal Access Token without any consent step. Attackers mint an unauthenticated code, lure a logged-in user to that URL, then retrieve the victim's PAT from the unauthenticated /api/v1/token endpoint to take over the account.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.4 Hardcoded Coordinator Secret Authentication Bypass via Socket.IO
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.4 contains a hardcoded default secret vulnerability in the /coordinator Socket.IO namespace that allows unauthenticated attackers to connect using the published coordinator-secret value. Attackers can emit READY_FOR_EXECUTION to retrieve decrypted run environment variables or send TASK_RUN_FAILED_TO_RUN and similar events to tamper with arbitrary runs.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Authentication Bypass via Hardcoded Default Secrets
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 self-hosted Docker Compose deployments using the default secrets from hosting/docker/.env.example allow authentication bypass because the hardcoded MAGIC_LINK_SECRET lets anyone forge valid magic link tokens. Unauthenticated attackers can log in as any email address, then reach Postgres, Redis, and ClickHouse with default credentials from runner containers on infrastructure networks, compromising all tenant data.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.5 Unauthenticated Realtime Stream Data Injection via Streams Endpoint
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the realtime streams POST handler that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject data into run streams. Attackers can send POST requests to /realtime/v1/streams/:runId/:streamId with a predictable run friendlyId to inject arbitrary data into any environment's realtime stream, including production.

t: Trigger.dev through 4.7.6 Missing Authentication in Supervisor Workload API
d: Trigger.dev through 4.7.6 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the supervisor workload server that allows workloads to manipulate runs belonging to other deployments without ownership verification. Attackers with network access and a valid run/snapshot pair can call the attempts/start endpoint to obtain resolved environment variables and run JWTs, or start, complete, and suspend other tenants' runs.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 SQL Injection via tags in Realtime Runs API
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the /realtime/v1/runs endpoint, which concatenates the unescaped tags query parameter into the ElectricSQL shape where clause and defeats the runtimeEnvironmentId tenant guard. Authenticated attackers holding any project API key with read:runs scope can append boolean conditions to stream TaskRun records, including payloads and metadata, from every organization on the same self-hosted instance.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0-rc.3 Path Traversal via Packets Presigned URL Endpoints
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0-rc.3 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the api/v1/packets and api/v2/packets endpoints that allows authenticated tenants to escape their object key prefix through an unsanitized filename splat segment. Attackers holding one valid API key can supply ../ sequences to obtain presigned GET or PUT URLs and read or overwrite other tenants' run payloads and outputs.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.6.2 Overly Broad Realtime Session Stream Credentials
d: Trigger.dev before 4.6.2 contains an authorization vulnerability that allows public-token holders with session write access to obtain environment-wide S2 stream credentials via session input initialization. Attackers can use the credential directly against the storage API to append, create, or trim other session and run streams, forging output or permanently deleting records.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Cross-Tenant SQL Injection via TSQL Window-Function Name
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the TSQL query compiler, which concatenates window-function names into generated ClickHouse SQL without allowlisting or escaping. Authenticated customers can submit a backtick-quoted identifier to POST /api/v1/query that injects a raw subquery outside the per-tenant WHERE guard, exfiltrating other organizations' analytics data.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 Blind SSRF via Alert-Channel Webhook URL
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to make the server send requests by setting unvalidated alert-channel webhook URLs. Attackers can create alert channels pointing to loopback, internal, or cloud metadata addresses, then trigger alerts to probe internal service reachability and send signed POST requests.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Cross-Environment Deployment Cancel via Cancel Endpoint
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows holders of lower-trust environment API keys to cancel other environments' deployments because DeploymentService.getDeployment scopes lookups by projectId only. Attackers with a dev, preview, or CI secret key can POST to the deployment cancel endpoint to cancel in-progress production deployments within the same project.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Cross-Organization Schedule Deletion via Unscoped friendlyId Lookup
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in DeleteTaskScheduleService and SetActiveOnTaskScheduleService that allows authenticated users to delete or disable other organizations' schedules. Attackers can send delete or disable actions through their own project's schedule route with a victim schedule friendlyId to destroy other organizations' IMPERATIVE cron schedules.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 Cross-Tenant Deployment Hijack via createDeploymentBackgroundWorkerV4
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in createDeploymentBackgroundWorkerV4 that resolves a WorkerDeployment by friendlyId alone, without environment, project, or organization scoping. Attackers holding only their own environment API key can POST to the deployment background-workers endpoint with a victim's deployment ID to re-point that in-progress deployment at a worker in the attacker's environment.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 Blind SSRF via Alert Channel Webhook URL
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated tenants to make the webapp server send POST requests to internal hosts by setting an unvalidated webhook alert channel URL. Attackers can point the webhook at internal services or cloud metadata addresses and trigger alerts to scan internal hosts, send state-changing POSTs, or reach IMDSv1 via redirects.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 Authorization Bypass via Alert Channels API
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows holders of capability-restricted user-actor tokens to create alert channels by using the legacy personal access token helper. Attackers with a read-only UAT can POST to the project alertChannels endpoint to create production webhook channels, routing future deployment and error alerts to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.10 Webhook SSRF Protection Bypass via 198.18.0.0/15 Range
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.10 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to bypass webhook SSRF protections by targeting the non-global 198.18.0.0/15 benchmarking range. Attackers can configure alert-channel webhooks pointing at internally routed services in this range, which isUnsafeIPv4 omits, to perform blind internal probing and limited state-changing POST requests.

t: Trigger.dev CLI before 4.5.9 Secret Exposure via Debug Deployment Logs
d: Trigger.dev CLI before 4.5.9 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes resolved environment secret values in debug deployment logs by serializing unredacted envVars. Attackers with access to terminal transcripts, CI debug logs, or support bundles can read the Starting buildWorker record to recover database connection strings and service credentials.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 CSRF via Slack OAuth Callback State
d: The Trigger.dev webapp before 4.5.12 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in its organization-level Slack OAuth flow, which uses the organization ID as the OAuth state without binding it to the initiating session. Attackers who know a target organization ID can trick an authenticated member into opening an unredeemed /integrations/slack/callback URL, connecting an attacker-controlled Slack workspace that may receive the organization's operational alerts.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 Authorization Bypass via Waitpoint Complete Route
d: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to complete another member's DEVELOPMENT environment waitpoint by skipping the per-user environment ownership check. Attackers who know a victim's waitpoint friendly ID can submit type=DATETIME or type=MANUAL with isTimeout to prematurely mark the pending waitpoint completed.

t: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.0 Dashboard Agent User Token Disclosure via Session Records
d: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Dashboard Agent input proxy that stores a delegated user-actor token in browser-readable session input records. Attackers holding a chat's public session token can read the in records endpoint to recover the token from payload.metadata.userActorToken and replay it for environment JWT exchange.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 Root Secret Disclosure via envvars API Endpoint
d: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/projects/:projectRef/envvars endpoint, which returns the environment's root API key as TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY for staging, production, and preview environments. Attackers holding a restricted read:envvars key can obtain the root secret and plaintext secrets, then trigger tasks and mint admin public JWTs.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 Missing Authorization via Waitpoint Token Wait Endpoint
d: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the waitpoint token wait endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to block runs belonging to other organizations. Attackers holding any secret API key can supply a victim run ID with their own waitpoint, causing that run to block indefinitely on a waitpoint the victim cannot complete, and can inject resume data into it.

t: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.2 Improper Authorization via snapshot-url Session Route
d: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the PUT snapshot-url session endpoint that allows public session token holders to obtain presigned S3 write URLs. End users can overwrite their own session's durable chat snapshot to forge the agent's conversation history, since the route lacks a secret-key-only check.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.7.0 Missing Authorization via Batch parentRunId Waitpoints
d: Trigger.dev before 4.7.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows holders of unrestricted environment API keys to block runs they do not own by supplying a foreign parentRunId to batch-creation endpoints. Attackers can send requests to POST /api/v3/batches or POST /api/v2/tasks/batch with resumeParentOnCompletion to suspend, indefinitely block, or inject errors into production or cross-organization runs.

t: Trigger.dev before 4.7.3 Tenant Filtering Bypass via Query Table Placeholders
d: Trigger.dev before 4.7.3 contains a tenant filtering bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' data by using placeholder table syntax in POST /api/v1/query. Attackers can submit queries with FROM {database.table} expressions, including within subqueries, to skip table allowlist and tenant filters and expose run metadata and payloads.

t: Snipe-IT before 8.7.0 SSRF Port Scanning via Webhook Testing Endpoint
d: Snipe-IT before 8.7.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the webhook testing feature that allows super-admin users to probe internal network addresses, including loopback and RFC1918 ranges. Attackers can point webhooks at internal hosts and ports, then compare 4xx versus 5xx responses from Test Webhooks to map open ports and active hosts.

t: SvelteKit 2.10.0 before 3.0.0 Path Traversal via vite preview on Windows
d: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) from 2.10.0 before 3.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the vite preview server on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files outside the prerendered output directory. Attackers who can reach the preview server through network access or a tunnel can send crafted requests to expose source code, configuration, or credentials readable by the server process.

t: SvelteKit before 3.0.0 SSRF via Redirects in Server-Side Self-Fetch Fallbacks
d: SvelteKit before 3.0.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to reach internal services because self-fetch fallbacks follow HTTP redirects automatically. Attackers can manipulate the Host or forwarded headers to point fallback requests at their server, which redirects them to internal services.

t: SvelteKit before 3.0.0 XSS via Cache-Control Header in Prerendered Pages
d: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) before 3.0.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in prerendered pages because a cache-control header value set via setHeaders is inserted without escaping into a <meta http-equiv="cache-control"> tag. An attacker who can influence that untrusted value at prerender time can break out of the content attribute and inject HTML or JavaScript that executes when users visit the page.

t: SvelteKit before 3.0.0 Open Redirect via Enhanced Form Actions
d: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) before 3.0.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in enhanced form actions (use:enhance) on routes accepting paths beginning with a double slash. Attackers can craft action paths starting with // that become protocol-relative URLs, causing non-redirect form results to navigate victims to attacker-controlled sites.

t: ArcadeDB before 26.10.1 RCE via Gremlin Groovy Engine Missing Authorization
d: ArcadeDB before 26.10.1 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated users, including read-only reader role holders, to execute Groovy code because GremlinQueryEngine.command() lacks scripting authorization checks. Attackers can submit Gremlin commands to the POST /api/v1/command/{database} endpoint when the Groovy engine is enabled to run OS commands as the server process user.

t: ArcadeDB from 26.2.1 before 26.10.1 Missing Authorization via Bolt Protocol
d: ArcadeDB from 26.2.1 before 26.10.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Bolt protocol handler that lets authenticated users read other databases' schema metadata. Attackers with credentials for one database can set the db field in RUN or BEGIN messages and call db.labels() or SHOW INDEXES to enumerate unauthorized schemas.

t: ArcadeDB 26.2.1 before 26.10.1 Bolt SHOW DATABASES Information Disclosure
d: ArcadeDB from 26.2.1 before 26.10.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Bolt protocol handler that allows authenticated users to enumerate all database names. Attackers with credentials for any single database can issue a SHOW DATABASES query over the Bolt port to reveal unauthorized database names, exposing tenant or project identifiers.

t: ArcadeDB from 26.8.1 before 26.10.1 Authorization Bypass via ALTER TYPE WITH
d: ArcadeDB from 26.8.1 before 26.10.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows read-only users to modify edge type lightweight and unique schema flags without UPDATE_SCHEMA permission. Attackers can send a bare ALTER TYPE edgeType WITH lightweight = true command over the HTTP, gRPC, or Bolt command API to persistently alter edge storage declarations.

t: vLLM 0.7.3 before 0.31.0 DoS via Unvalidated mm_processor_kwargs
d: vLLM from 0.7.3 before 0.31.0 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows remote clients to control multimodal processor parameters by supplying per-request mm_processor_kwargs. Attackers can set large image size, patch count, crop count, or frame count values in Isaac, InternVL, H2OVL, and other processors to exhaust memory and terminate the shared server.

t: vLLM before 0.31.0 Cross-Request Cache Aliasing via EXIF ImageID and Prefix-Cache Keys
d: vLLM before 0.31.0 contains a cache aliasing vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to collide shared cache keys by supplying caller-controlled values such as EXIF ImageID or cache_salt. Attackers can set a UUID EXIF ImageID to receive another request's cached processed media, or match cache_salt to a LoRA name to reuse first-block KV state.

t: vLLM 0.7.3 before 0.31.0 RCE via mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision
d: vLLM from 0.7.3 before 0.31.0 forwards the request-supplied mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision to Transformers AutoProcessor.from_pretrained, letting clients select which revision of a model's dynamic processor code is imported when trust_remote_code is enabled. An attacker controlling a revision in the served model repository can send a multimodal request to the unauthenticated /tokenize endpoint to execute arbitrary Python in the vLLM API process.

t: vLLM 0.25.0 before 0.31.0 MOSS-Audio Memory Exhaustion via /tokenize mm_processor_kwargs
d: vLLM after 0.24.0 and before 0.31.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in MOSS-Audio model serving that caches a processor for every distinct request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs value in an unbounded dictionary. Unauthenticated attackers can send distinct or oversized mel_config values to the /tokenize endpoint, which bypasses --api-key, to exhaust host memory and crash the API process.

t: vLLM before 0.31.0 Denial of Service via min_tokens in /inference/v1/generate
d: vLLM before 0.31.0 skips the min_tokens <= max_tokens check for /inference/v1/generate requests with a null max_tokens, so the EngineCore input thread later dies on an uncaught VLLMValidationError while /health still returns 200. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send one request with an oversized min_tokens to hang all subsequent generation requests until manual restart.

t: vLLM before 0.31.0 Remote Engine Crash via Forged Multimodal UUID
d: vLLM before 0.31.0 uses a client-supplied multimodal uuid verbatim as cache identity with no consistency check on cache hits, allowing engine crashes. Unauthenticated attackers can desynchronize the P0/P1 processor caches to trigger a fatal token-placeholder mismatch, killing the entire serving instance until restarted.

t: vLLM before 0.31.0 Stale allowed_token_ids Mask via InputBatch.condense
d: vLLM before 0.31.0 contains a cross-request mask leak in InputBatch.condense() that allows remote attackers to constrain other clients' outputs by leaving stale allowed_token_ids rows. Attackers can submit concurrent constrained generate requests, including via unauthenticated /invocations, so recycled batch slots apply their token allowlist to victims' unrestricted requests.

t: WWBN AVideo before 24.0 CSRF via Legacy Playlist and Video Endpoints
d: WWBN AVideo before 24.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in legacy endpoints like playlistStatus.php that bypass the .json.php-only autoCSRFGuard() check. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a page with an auto-submitting form to make private playlists public, remove playlist videos, or forge video suggestions.

t: FreeRDP 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 Proxy Improper TLS Certificate Validation
d: FreeRDP from 2.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in its proxy that accepts untrusted target TLS certificates when no verification module is configured. Network-positioned attackers can intercept the proxy's outbound connection and present a self-signed, wrong-hostname certificate to impersonate the RDP target and receive proxied session data.

t: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 null-pointer dereference via emulated smartcard
d: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.32.0 contains a null-pointer dereference in the smartcard emulation backend that accepts a null per-reader name in SCardGetStatusChange requests. A malicious RDP server can send a crafted reader-state entry with a null szReader, causing strcmp or _wcscmp to crash the client process.

t: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 Heap Buffer Overflow via rdpsnd_server_select_format
d: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in the server-side rdpsnd channel because an integer wraparound in rdpsnd_server_select_format() DVI_ADPCM block-alignment arithmetic bypasses validation. A malicious RDP client can send two SNDC_FORMATS PDUs with an nBlockAlign too small for nChannels, causing an unbounded heap write during server audio playback, potentially enabling code execution.

t: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 Android Client Heap OOB Read via Graphics Pipeline
d: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the Android client that allows malicious RDP servers to read beyond surface buffers by supplying unvalidated mappedWidth and mappedHeight values. Attackers can send a crafted RDPGFX_MAP_SURFACE_TO_WINDOW_PDU with oversized dimensions, causing android_UpdateWindowFromSurface to copy heap memory beyond the allocation, leading to crashes or memory disclosure.

t: Vulnerability in FreeRDP
d: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read in WinPR's clipboard PNG-to-CF_DIB synthesis because winpr_read_png_from_buffer() allocates a bit-packed buffer for PNGs with bit depth below 8, while winpr_bitmap_write_buffer() copies rows assuming one byte per pixel. A malicious RDP server can send a crafted low-bit-depth PNG clipboard payload that, when pasted by the victim, discloses megabytes of heap memory.

t: FreeRDP 3.32.0 Use-After-Free via drdynvc Virtual Channel PDU
d: FreeRDP 3.32.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the drdynvc channel that frees a pool-owned stream with the owned-stream deallocator when totalLength is smaller than the chunk size. A malicious RDP server can send a single well-formed Virtual Channel PDU to trigger the free and crash the client during teardown.

t: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via RD Gateway Consent Message
d: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 on Windows contains a heap out-of-bounds read in client_cli_present_gateway_message that passes a byte count as wide-character printf precision. A malicious RD Gateway can send pre-authentication consent or service messages, causing the client to read twice the buffer size, leaking heap memory or crashing.

t: Astral uv through 0.8.21 Path Traversal via Symlinks in Sdist Tar Extraction
d: Astral uv before 0.8.22 contains a path traversal vulnerability in source distribution (sdist) tar extraction that allows a specially crafted sequence of symlinks to redirect file writes outside the intended extraction prefix. Attackers can publish a malicious sdist that, when installed by a victim, writes arbitrary files to filesystem locations outside the installation prefix.

t: Vyper before 0.3.0 Memory Corruption via Internal Function Calls in Arrays
d: Vyper from 0.1.0b4 before 0.3.0 contains a memory corruption vulnerability caused by an incorrect stack tip pointer when internal function calls are performed inside arrays. Contracts placing internal calls in nested array elements, external call arguments, struct literals, or raw_log topics can have memory corrupted, producing incorrect contract behavior.

t: Vyper before 0.2.9 Incorrect RETURNDATASIZE in create_forwarder_to Proxies
d: Vyper before 0.2.9 deploys forwarder proxies through the built-in create_forwarder_to function that report a fixed 4096-byte RETURNDATASIZE rather than the actual return data size. Calls through these proxies can yield corrupted data when a function returns more than 4096 bytes without return data sanitation, and fail strict return-size checks such as SafeERC20.safeTransfer.

t: Vyper 0.2.13 before 0.2.15 Storage Corruption via @nonreentrant Decorator
d: Vyper from 0.2.13 before 0.2.15 allocates storage slots for @nonreentrant reentrancy locks at the same locations as contract storage variables.
